newsitem.title: UK: India sugar output reaches 12.77 mln T - Czarnikow.
newsitem.headline: India sugar output reaches 12.77 mln T - Czarnikow.

text.p: Indian sugar production had reached 12.77 million tonnes (tel quel) by mid-June, more than three million tonnes down from a year earlier, Czarnikow Sugar said in its latest report on Thursday.

"Very little additional sugar is expected to be produced from the current crop and the final total is unlikely to exceed 12.8 million tonnes, whereas late session operations took last season's total to 16.45 million tonnes," Czarnikow said.
The fall in Indian sugar production is one of the major factors contributing to a forward outlook of tightening supplies over the next one to two seasons, Czarnikow said.
"There seems little prospect that those farmers which have switched land to alternative crops have returned to cane for next season."
"Consumption on the other hand has progressed at higher than its historical rate."
Demand was on course to reach 14.0 million tonnes by the end of the season at the end of September.

"It is not likely that further exports will materialise as domestic prices have been firming in recent years while world market prices have not risen to the levels likely to draw out fresh export commitments."
